ledger.x: 1177: the Duchy of Kalisz is created in the partition of the Duchy of Greater Poland.
1191: Kalisz becomes a separate duchy again.
1194: Odon dies and Kalisz returns to Greater Poland.
1207: Greater Poland divides into Poznań, Gniezno and Kalisz again.
1229: Władysław Odonic takes the whole of Greater Poland.
1234: Greater Poland divides again (infobox window 1234-1238); the body text only says Henry I the Bearded 'began conquering most of Odonic's lands from 1234 onward'.
1238: end of the infobox division window 1234-1238; the page gives no sentence for the reunification.
1247: a division gives Bolesław the Pious Kalisz.
1250: end of the infobox division window 1247-1250; no sentence on the page.
1253: Bolesław the Pious is back at Kalisz.
1257: end of the infobox division window 1253-1257; no sentence on the page.
1277: the last division of Greater Poland (infobox window 1277-1279).
1279: Kalisz is united with Gniezno and Poznań.
1279: the Duchy of Kalisz ends; its land passes to the reconstituted Duchy of Greater Poland under Przemysł II (last duke of Kalisz, 1273-1279).

wars.name: Odon's revolt against Mieszko III the Old
wars.outcome: Odon backed the 1177-79 challenge to his father, expelled him from the Greater Polish lands in 1179, and was forced out of Poznań in 1181; Mieszko III seized Gniezno and Kalisz in 1181.

wars.name: Władysław III Spindleshanks against Władysław Odonic for Greater Poland
wars.outcome: From 1217 Spindleshanks, reconciled with Leszek I and Henry I the Bearded, expelled his nephew Odonic; after Leszek's death in 1227 Odonic won, taking all of Greater Poland in 1229 while Spindleshanks fled to Silesia.

certainty.note: Neither page describes the duchy's borders, and it was repeatedly joined to and split from Greater Poland; every frontier is approximate.
